generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the herb base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the herb program gave as defaults until then.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: DELTA Orobanchaceae (read 2026-10-16): leaves small, alternate, spiral (often scale-like). Would otherwise inherit decussate.

traits.note: Jepson eFlora's account of the family (Wetherwax), as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): flowers strongly bilateral; corolla of 5 united petals, two-lipped, the upper lip 2-lobed (a beak, the galea, in paintbrushes), the lower 3-lobed; stamens 4, didynamous, on the corolla tube; ovary superior, of 2 carpels.

traits.woodiness.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 327 Orobanchaceae (broomrapes), with the green half-parasites he keeps in Scrophulariaceae (Castilleja, Pedicularis), which APG joins as Orobanchaceae: herbs; leaves or scales alternate; stipules absent; fruit a capsule opening by two valves.

Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.leaf_division.note: APG's Orobanchaceae is mostly the half-parasites that the floras kept in Scrophulariaceae (Pedicularis, Castilleja, Euphrasia, Rhinanthus, Melampyrum) with the old broomrapes, whose leaves are scales. Watson and Dallwitz (DELTA data, family Orobanchaceae, the broomrapes alone): leaves simple and entire. Pedicularis, the largest genus, has pinnately lobed to divided leaves, and Castilleja's are entire or lobed: so leaves simple, unlobed usually and lobed often, the lobes pinnate (inferred from the genera, not traced).

traits.inflorescence.note: Wikipedia Orobanchaceae (read 2026-10-17): flowers in racemes, in spikes, or single at the stem tip; ~2,000 spp. Wikipedia Pedicularis (read 2026-10-17): 600+ spp, bees work its spikes, so the largest genus (~30% of the family) counts as spike, with Castilleja, Euphrasia and Orobanche (spikes or spike-like racemes) behind it; single terminal flowers are confined to small holoparasite genera (Aeginetia, Christisonia). Re-ranks the earlier value, from plant-systematics-simpson, whose top states were tied.

traits.perennation.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Orobanchaceae: how its perennial herbs last from year to year (character 25), coded usually a rhizome, rarely tubers. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 25 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.
